name: Oirad-Kalmyk-Darkhat
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: kalm1243 (Oirad-Kalmyk-Darkhat, Mongolic) is not in the catalog. The single sweep item, Dirim 2010 ('Wenn man mit Akzent spricht...'), is a false positive: a German education-science essay on migrant accents and linguicism; the Glottolog record (opened, saved) shows both the language link ([xal] 'computerized assignment from \"wenn\"') and the hhtype ('grammar_sketch, computerized assignment from \"sprache\"') are automatic. Not relevant, priority none, no copy needed. the working files already held (from an earlier audit) open copies of Saj 2009 (ALP V(2), Kalmyk grammatical sketch) and Popov 1847; I read their stress passages: Saj 2009 p. 630 states non-contrastive, always-final stress (shifting to the penult only when a final schwa drops by sandhi) and rejects Pjurbeev 1997's 'mobile stress' from field data; Popov 1847 §42 pp. 20-21 says short stress is always on the last syllable, 'long stress' (= vowel length) medial/final. Best statement: Saj 2009 p. 630 (fixed final).

new_statements.quote: Ударение в калмыцком языке не имеет смыслоразличительной функции. Фонетически ударным всегда является последний слог слова⁶. В случае, если ожидаемый в последнем слоге гласный «шва» выпадает из-за сандхиальных явлений, ударение автоматически переходит на предшествующий слог. [fn. 6:] В литературе калмыцкое ударение иногда трактуется как подвижное [Пюрбеев 1997: 76], однако нашими полевыми материалами эта точка зрения не подтверждается.
new_statements.translation: Stress in Kalmyk has no meaning-distinguishing function. Phonetically, the last syllable of the word is always stressed [fn. 6]. If the schwa vowel expected in the last syllable is dropped because of sandhi phenomena, the stress automatically shifts to the preceding syllable. [fn. 6:] In the literature Kalmyk stress is sometimes treated as mobile [Pjurbeev 1997: 76], but this view is not confirmed by our field materials.
new_statements.citation: Saj, S. S. 2009. Grammatičeskij očerk kalmyckogo jazyka [A sketch of Kalmyk grammar]. In S. S. Saj, V. V. Baranova & N. V. Serdobol'skaja (eds.), Issledovanija po grammatike kalmyckogo jazyka (Acta Linguistica Petropolitana. Trudy Instituta lingvističeskix issledovanij, Vol. V, part 2), 622–709. Sankt-Peterburg: Nauka.
new_statements.locator: p. 630, §3 'Fonotaktika, morfonologija i nesegmentnye fonetičeskie zakonomernosti', with footnote 6 (printed page = PDF page 630 of 895)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (895 pp.) and extracted PDF page 630 with extracted text. It is printed page 630 of S. S. Saj, "Grammatičeskij očerk kalmyckogo jazyka", §3 "Fonotaktika, morfonologija i nesegmentnye fonetičeskie zakonomernosti". The quoted passage is there verbatim: "Ударение в калмыцком языке не имеет смысло-различительной функции. Фонетически ударным всегда является последний слог слова6. В случае, если ожидаемый в последнем слоге гласный «шва» выпадает из-за сандхиальных явлений, ударение автоматически переходит на предшествующий слог." and footnote 6: "В литературе калмыцкое ударение иногда трактуется как подвижное [Пюрбеев 1997: 76], однако нашими полевыми материалами эта точка зрения не подтве…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Non-contrastive word stress always on the final syllable of the word (including a final schwa); when that final schwa is deleted by sandhi, stress falls on the new final (originally penultimate) syllable — i.e. stress stays word-final after deletion.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the schwa-sandhi case (stress moves to the preceding syllable when the final schwa drops). Footnote 6 records that Pjurbeev 1997: 76 treats Kalmyk stress as mobile, which Saj's field data do not confirm. Elsewhere in the volume Baranova (pp. 258, 271, 304) notes that grammaticalised auxiliaries lose their own stress and cliticise onto the preceding verb form.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (phonetic word); based on 2006–2008 fieldwork in the Dörbet (dürvüd) dialect area (Ergeninskij and Tugtun, Ketčenerovskij district, Kalmykia), with reference to descriptions of the literary language. Popov 1847 §42 (pp. 20–21) already states that 'short stress' is always on the last syllable (his 'long stress' is vowel length).
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding statement is for Kalmyk of the Republic of Kalmykia (Russia), specifically field data from the Dörbet (dürvüd/derbet) dialect (Ketčenerovskij district) checked against descriptions of literary Kalmyk; Glottolog's kalm1243 'Oirad-Kalmyk-Darkhat' also covers Xinjiang/Mongolian Oirat and Darkhat, which this source does not describe (Glottolog 5.1 lists no separate dialect glottocodes on the languoid page as fetched sources). Popov 1847 describes 19th-century Volga Kalmyk.

If the schwa vowel expected in the last syllable is dropped because of sandhi phenomena, stress automatically shifts to the preceding syllable. new_statements.citation: Saj, S. S. 2009. Grammatičeskij očerk kalmyckogo jazyka. In S. S. Saj, V. V. Baranova & N. V. Serdobol'skaja (eds.), Issledovanija po grammatike kalmyckogo jazyka (Acta Linguistica Petropolitana V(2)), 622–709. St Petersburg: Nauka.
new_statements.locator: §3 'Fonotaktika, morfonologija i nesegmentnye fonetičeskie zakonomernosti', p. 630, incl. footnote 6
new_statements.reading: Fixed, non-contrastive final (ultimate) word stress in Kalmyk, based on the authors' own fieldwork; the only deviation is a surface shift to the penult when the final schwa is deleted by sandhi (i.e. stress stays on the last realized syllable). Explicitly rejects the 'mobile stress' account of Pjurbeev 1997. Consistent with Popov 1847 §42 (short stress always on the last syllable). Language is not in the catalog, so there is no deciding source to supersede; this is the recommended deciding source if a record is created (kind: fixed final).

sources.citation: Popov, Aleksandr. 1847. Grammatika kalmyckago jazyka. Kazan': Universitetskaja tipografija. 409 pp.
sources.quote: § 42. Удареніе голоса въ калмыцкихъ словахъ бываетъ двоякое: короткое и долгое; первое употребляется всегда на послѣднемъ слогѣ, напр. ельчі посланникъ, зарликъ повелѣніе, ябуху ходить, поступать, послѣднее же въ срединѣ и концѣ словъ. Для означенія долгаго ударенія калмыки имѣютъ особенный знакъ ... приставляемый ими въ нѣкоторыхъ словахъ съ правой стороны къ гласной буквѣ того слога, на которомъ ударяется голосъ
sources.note: §42, pp. 20–21 (PDF pp. 40–41): 'Удареніе голоса въ калмыцкихъ словахъ бываетъ двоякое: короткое и долгое; первое употребляется всегда на послѣднемъ слогѣ, напр. ельчи посланникъ, зарликъ повелѣніе, ябуху ходить... послѣднее же въ срединѣ и концѣ словъ' — 'short stress' is always on the last syllable; 'long stress' is in fact vowel length, marked in the Clear script by a diacritic.
